key_insight: AEAPTMS passivation makes perovskite surfaces electronically more uniform, reducing grain-boundary barriers and producing a larger, faster-stabilizing surface photovoltage.
engineering_relevance: This suggests amino-silane passivation can improve carrier landscape stability in perovskite solar cells, helping reduce photovoltage losses at the device-relevant nanoscale.
method: Amplitude-modulated Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) to map dark CPD and illuminated SPV
Compare passivated vs. unpassivated mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite thin films
Separate grain-boundary and grain-interior responses and probe wavelength-dependent SPV
evidence_signal: Dark CPD distribution narrowed from ~45.7 to ~14.6 mV, SPV increased from ~345 to ~417 mV, and stabilization time constant dropped from ~840 to ~470 s after AEAPTMS treatment.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on thin-film nanoscale measurements, so translation to full device stability and long-term operational performance still needs validation.
paper_title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
